replies.text:
Check against commonly-missed threats:

1. Automated abuse (brute force, flooding, scraping): the design names no sign-in, form, page or API — it only says "The app sends push notifications that include the full order contents and delivery address." Flooding of the send path depends on how the trigger is built, which the design does not state. Not reportable.
2. Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content: nothing in the design describes any internal console or review screen. Not present.
3. Delete/moderate/refund/approve/role-change/money actions without a record: the design states no such action and no actor; "Notifications show on the lock screen by default" is the only behaviour given. Not present.
4. Personal pages/documents cached by browsers, proxies or CDNs: no web page, document or HTTP response is described — delivery is push only. Not present.
5. Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/spreadsheet exports, emails, headers or another interpreting system: the only onward system named is the push payload path, already covered by listed threat 3 ("Order contents and addresses handed to Apple/Google push infrastructure in the payload"). Covered.

Single-reviewer threats: #1 and #4 both restate the unauthenticated/unverified send path already covered by listed threat 1 and depend on unstated implementation of recipient resolution; #2 flooding depends on a replayable event the design never describes; #3 watch/mirroring/notification-history fan-out is the same weakness and the same harm as listed threat 2, a sub-case rather than a gap. None qualify.
